No, but it is related to something specific.

File creation and deletion is governed by the applicable write bit of the parent folder, not of the file. This is because the parent folder is actually just a special file with a list of the files contained therein and their inode addresses.

The warning on rm for a read only file is just a courtesy, not an enforcement of permissions.
